methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Airship Industries is a pre-seed stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The available comparable universe consists of 8 private companies operating in this space, including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro. No public companies trade in this narrow subsector, limiting the availability of market-based valuation anchors.

The peer-median approach was deemed inapplicable due to insufficient comparable data. While 7 same-sector peers exist within Drones & Autonomous, none satisfied the filtering criteria of matching stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—a minimum of 3 datapoints per filter was required. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of pre-seed venture valuations across Drones & Autonomous and related markets.

Without a sufficiently narrow peer set or triangulated methods yielding quantifiable results, this analysis cannot support a specific valuation range at this time. Key uncertainties preventing a determination include the absence of pre-seed or adjacent-stage comparables with documented terms, the wide variance in business models and capital efficiency across the 8 private peers, and the lack of public market comparables for calibration. A valuation determination would require either additional pre-seed stage data within the Drones & Autonomous sector or alternative approaches such as venture capital method modeling with disclosed assumptions on revenue trajectory and exit multiples.
